lines: The cup of the cyathium is formed by an

It encloses one central female flower and
steps.why: Morphologically the cup is BRACTS, not petals or a receptacle - fused bracts (an involucre). That is the tested word.
common_mistakes: Calling the cup a corolla or a receptacle. It is made of fused bracts.
steps.memory_tip: Cyathium cup = bracts joined into a cup (involucre).
steps.margin_note: The phrase 'involucre of bracts' is the mark; the flower contents are a bonus line.

lines.text: Cyathium is found in the family

steps.why: Cyathium is the marker inflorescence of one family - Euphorbiaceae; naming it is the second mark.
common_mistakes: Writing Asteraceae. The head belongs to Asteraceae; the cyathium belongs to Euphorbiaceae.
steps.memory_tip: Cyathium sits with Euphorbia - both start rare letters, C and E of Euphorbiaceae.
steps.margin_note: Family name alone earns it; an example genus strengthens the line.
